title: Transport
subtitle: catch the bus, miss the train, fares and journeys
summary: Name the vehicles on the road and use the right verbs and nouns to talk about buses, trains, planes and taxis.

lesson.heading: Vehicles
rows: it carries people round a town
a comfortable bus for long journeys
a big vehicle that carries goods
you ride it and use your legs
lesson.note: **Vehicle** is the general word for all types of road transport.

lesson.heading: Travelling around
lesson.note: With a bicycle we say **go by bike**, **cycle** or **ride a bike**, and you **get on** and **off** it.

lesson.heading: Talking about journeys
lesson.text: We **get** or **catch** a bus or a train, and we **miss** it if we don't catch it. The **fare** is the money you pay; the **journey** is the travelling itself.

examples.text: I go to work by bus. It's only three **stops**.
We **got the train** to Cardiff, but the **journey** was terrible.
When the bus **fares** went up last month, my dad started **cycling** to work.
I **got out of** the taxi and almost walked away without paying the **fare**.
We were going to get the train to Paris, but in the end we decided to **fly**.

lesson.text: Say *It was a good **journey***, not ~~It was a good travel~~. *Travel* is not normally a countable noun.

lesson.heading: Is public transport convenient?
lesson.text: **Public transport** means buses and trains for people to use. If a bus stop is **convenient**, it is near or easy to use; if it is half a mile **away**, it is not.

examples.text: The nearest bus stop is half a mile **away**.
I often have to wait in a **queue** for twenty minutes.
I've got a bus stop **round the corner**.
Buses **run** every ten minutes and they're usually **reliable**.

lesson.heading: Tickets and complaints
lesson.text: A **return** is a ticket for a journey to a place and back; a **single** is one way only. A **season ticket** lets you travel many times in a period without paying each time.

examples.text: A **return** to London is forty pounds.
I've got a **season ticket**, and that makes it cheaper.
People are always **complaining about** the bus service.
examples.note: complain about = say you are not satisfied with

examples.text: I made a **complaint** about the service.
If I **miss** my train, I have to wait half an hour for the next one.

exercises.prompt: You mustn't ___ a motorbike without a helmet in the UK.
exercises.explanation: We ride a motorbike or a bicycle; we drive a car.

exercises.prompt: She told him to ___ the car and fasten his seat belt.
exercises.explanation: You get in and out of a car or taxi, but on and off a bus, train or plane.

exercises.prompt: The ___ to the airport takes half an hour.
exercises.explanation: We say a good or bad journey, not a good travel.

exercises.prompt: Trains to the airport ___ every half hour.
exercises.explanation: Buses and trains run every ten minutes, every half hour, etc.

exercises.prompt: The ___ didn't want to fly the plane in such bad weather.
They left a bit late and ___ the bus.
exercises.explanation: You miss a bus or train when you don't catch it.

exercises.prompt: I see that train ___ are going up again.
exercises.explanation: The fare is the price of a journey.

exercises.prompt: We must get ___ the bus at the next stop.
exercises.explanation: You get on and off a bus; you get in and out of a car.

exercises.prompt: Match each vehicle with its description.

pairs.right: a comfortable bus for long journeys
a big vehicle that carries goods
you ride it using your legs

exercises.prompt: The flight was fine but we had a terrible ___ from the airport to our hotel.
exercises.explanation: A journey is the travelling from one place to another.

exercises.prompt: The public transport isn't very ___ because the nearest bus stop is two kilometres away.
exercises.explanation: Convenient = near or easy to use.

exercises.prompt: The train station is just round the ___ from where I live.
Buses are not very ___ . Sometimes they come every five minutes, but other times you wait forty minutes.
Train fares are crazy: a ___ to Glasgow costs more than two singles.
exercises.explanation: A return is a ticket for a journey to a place and back.

exercises.prompt: I use the trains every day for work, so I've got a ___ ticket.
exercises.explanation: A season ticket lets you travel many times without paying each time.

exercises.prompt: Your train is going to depart from ___ six at 10:25.
exercises.explanation: At a train station you wait on a platform.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a complaint.
exercises.answer: People are always complaining about the bus service.
exercises.explanation: Complain about something = say you are not satisfied with it.

exercises.statement: A taxi rank is the place where you wait for a taxi.
exercises.explanation: Correct. You take a taxi from a taxi rank.
